findings.reason: it changes which node lands for this repair, making the single shared git-invocation helper the delivered owner (with the status call sites routed through it) rather than an open follow-on behind a stop-gap the plan already names as the tempting wrong choice.
findings.text: three parallel git-subprocess wrappers (`routing.py:242 _git`, `node.py:650/670 _git_answer/_output`, `dispatch.py:3948 _worktree_git_read`) carry the same invocation over the same machinery with no owning helper; the plan itself calls this "no common boundary" and notes the package contains no `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS`/`--no-optional-locks` anywhere, yet the change it schedules to land now is env-per-site, which preserves all three paths and predicts a fourth

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan's repairs are edits to existing deep modules (runs.py, cli.py, recovery.py, ticker.py, dispatch.py) rather than new shallow surfaces, and the one place it considers a new module (a shared git-invocation helper) it reasons explicitly about depth: one helper carrying the env versus per-site edits, rejecting the many-wrappers shape as "exactly the decay the env was meant to design out."
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan diagnoses 32 `subprocess.run` git calls across six crew modules with no shared boundary, naming three parallel wrappers over the same machinery (`routing.py:242 _git`, `node.py:650/670 _git_answer/_output`, `dispatch.py:3948 _worktree_git_read`), but its scheduled repair is the per-site env stop-gap, which leaves the fork in place.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan ran three reuse maps covering all 35 unlanded measure rows across the pending sections, each with verdicts and file:line citations held to independent scored review (79/78/78 of 100), and the mechanisms it names exist: `_record_producer_running` (reckon/crew/runs.py:2413), `_reconcile_watch_record` (runs.py:2478), `_resolved_gc_repo` (reckon/cli.py:1348) all resolve at the reviewed head.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — where the plan contemplates a thin stop-gap (setting `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` at the three existing git wrappers instead of adding a shared one), it states why the machinery is being touched that way and what it leaves open, requiring the stop-gap to be recorded as a stop-gap "not as the repair." A wrapper with its reason stated is not the finding the item describes.
